scope: Focused documentary audit of virtualization management architecture, roles, resource controls and learner/operator interaction patterns.
method: Read-only HTTPS retrieval, inspection of first-party text and project README, canonical/meta redirect resolution, and response SHA-256 recording. No platform installations, logins, VM provisioning, management-API mutation, backup restoration, or host/network changes were performed.

sources.title: Proxmox VE Administration Guide
sources.evidence_type: first-party documentation/project source retrieved and read; no authenticated product operation executed
supports: Proxmox VE documents QEMU/KVM and container management, browser interface, roles/ACLs, API tokens, resource pools, templates/cloud-init, network/storage management, task identifiers/logs and backup/restore.
Privilege-separated API-token permissions intersect token and user permissions.
The guide identifies an AGPLv3 licence and currently lists x86_64 plus aarch64 on NVIDIA Grace Hopper/Vera as supported host architectures; this does not establish Raspberry Pi support.
Resource-pool permission grouping alone is not evidence of the specific aggregate tenant quota policy proposed for the course.
sources.limitation: Moving documentation/reference version; pin and exercise the chosen release before using it as a course execution contract.

sources.title: Incus documentation overview
sources.evidence_type: first-party documentation/project source retrieved and read; no authenticated product operation executed
supports: Incus is a Linux system-container and virtual-machine manager built around a REST API.
The project explicitly identifies its licence as Apache 2.
Full local daemon/socket access can permit actions equivalent to host-root access; UI restrictions cannot replace daemon permissions.

sources.title: Incus projects
sources.evidence_type: first-party documentation/project source retrieved and read; no authenticated product operation executed
supports: Projects isolate instances and optionally images/profiles/networks/storage.
Confined projects and restricted certificates support multiple users, including laboratory use.
Full incus-admin access differs from a confined project and can grant host-root-equivalent capabilities.

access_limits: The guessed Cockpit feature-virtualmachines guide URL returned 404; the official application catalog and project README were used for supported capability claims.
The old Cockpit privileges URL returned an HTML meta redirect without substantive page text. Its canonical target on docs.cockpit-project.org was retrieved and inspected.
The Incus COPYING file was also retrieved during research; the referenced overview already explicitly states Apache 2 licensing, so the final fourth Incus reference covers project limits instead.
Current latest/main documentation can describe capabilities or requirements that differ from an installed or LTS release.
Public documentation does not identify which hypervisor a particular institution uses, prove all UI behaviour, demonstrate live permission enforcement, or establish hardware capacity.
validation_scope: Four comparison rows and proposed practical acceptance checks; no product comparison benchmark.
Guest SSH, guest-root permissions, VM API ownership and hypervisor/host administrator authority are distinct.
Proxmox pool grouping, Incus project limits, OpenStack quotas and Cockpit OS privileges are compared on their documented terms rather than treated as equivalent tenant systems.
Real host allocation, rollback, isolation, quota race, cleanup and restore behaviour remains a version-pinned lab implementation gate.
